x: Our Marathon champion, Macdonald, despite a bad spell at about forty miles when he was nearly caught by George Chantler, finished very strongly, and George running his usual steady race also did very well indeed to finish inside seven hours.
The promoters very sportingly delayed the start to enable MacDonald, who had arrived late, to take part, and we finally got away at 2-45p.m.
MacDonald and W. Wortley who had finished second last year.
It was good to see our London to Brighton men, Alan Bishop, MacDonald and Wortley sharpening up early in the season, it is hoped they will soon be starting their long preparation.

Macdonald and Footer couldn't have supplied enough superlatives to sum up my feelings. Each stride felt as though it would be my last, I resolved this would be my final road race, wished I had never been a runner and cursed myself for ever getting into the team.

2.0 ALL OUR YESTERDAYS Tom Carter Edward Stimpson Tom Morell Ernie Duffett George Chantler 7.45 TOP TEAM Macdonald, Baker, Piddington Plummer. 10.0 LATE NIGHT EXTRA or NIGHT RIDE with Peter Hillier & Company
